newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Commonwealth Bank has responded to the Finance Sector Union's enterprise bargaining demands by offering its workers non-union individual employment contracts. This is one of the most significant attempts by a major employer to overcome the power of unions by taking advantage of the Federal Government's non-union contracts legislation, introduced in March. Page 1.

As debate grows in Australia over the relationship between jobs growth and labour market flexibility, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development has found there is no clear link between a nation's collective wage bargaining system and its employment performance. The report also found the income gap between Australia's top and bottom earners has widened in the 10 years to 1995. Page 3.

German investment in Australia has risen by 45 per cent in the past two years to A$4.3 billion as a result of an effort to turn Australia into a gateway into Asia. Germany's biggest bank, Deutsche Bank AG will expand its Sydney workforce by 500 to 1500, and plans to shift its regional marketing operations and Australian dollar funds management to Sydney from London and Singapore. Page 3

New Workplace Relations and Small Business Minister Peter Reith yesterday promised to restore the relationship between the Government and the small business sector, and said he is open to the recommendations of a recent parliamentary report on Australia's fair trading laws, of which the big business chambers have expressed concerns. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The demolition by implosion of the Royal Canberra Hospital showered debris over thousands of spectators up to 500 metres from the site yesterday, killing a 12-year-old girl and injuring at least nine others. The Australian Capital Territory Government had encouraged spectators to attend, assured debris would spread only 10 metres from the site. ACT Chief Minister Kate Carnell has ordered an investigation into the disaster. Page 1.

The Howard Government will reassess Australia's relationship with Cambodia at Cabinet meetings today and tomorrow. Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said the meetings would discuss defence co-operation, whether to recognise the Hun Sen regime, and if aid payents should continue. Australia's ambassador to Cambodia Tony Kevin is seeking assurances on human rights and free elections. Page 1.

The Federal Cabinet will begin a review of its industry assistance policy today amid pressure over Australia's high unemployment rate. The Cabinet meeting will focus on information technology, telecommunications, and on-line industries, and will consider incentives to attract new industries and create jobs. Page 1.

An Australian Tax Office review has found that the Internet poses a threat to the country's indirect tax base. The soon-to-be-released report will show a gap in Australia's indirect tax base developing into the next century as businesses switch to Internt services which are not currently taxed. The Federal Government is expected to use the report to push for a Goods and Services Tax at the next election. Page 3
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Capital Territory Government, police and coronial inquiries have begun following the death of a 12-year-old girl after she was struck by debris from the demolition of the Royal Canberra Hospital yesterday. Thousands of spectators had gathered o the southern shore of Lake Burley Griffin to watch the supposedly safe implosion, which sent chunks of debris flying hundreds of metres through the air. Page 1.

Australian Council of Trade Unions president Jennie George said yesterday the strike at Rio Tinto's Hunter Valley Number 1 coal mine could escalate into a national confrontation involving the wharves and other industries. The Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union has been paying the striking workers for the duration of the five-week strike, with the final payout possibly more than A$3 million if the industrial action lasts more than three months, as union officials predict. Page 1.

Blacktown police would not confirm last night reports that the deaths of a woman and her two sons in a swimming pool were a double-murder suicide, but the deaths are being treated as suspicious. Blacktown police Inspector John Ferguson said a husband and wife returned to their Seven Hills home to find the woman's sister and her sons face down in the pool. Page 3.

Australian Council of Trade Unions president Jennie George said yesterday the threat of lower wages to help solve the unemployment problem signalled more industrial relations reform. George said the Howard Government would like to cut the minimum wage, whch leaves families with A$308 after tax. Page 3.
THE AGE

A 12-year-old girl was killed and another nine people injured when the demolition of the old Canberra hospital building went wrong yesterday, sending debris flying hundreds of metres through the air, and into the crowd of thousands who had gathered to wath the spectacle. The scattering of the debris occurred when a part of the building exploded instead of collapsing inwards. Page 1.

Australian Council of Trade Unions president Jennie George has proposed an employment levy to fund the possible compulsory employment of young people by large companies. The idea, and a scheme for job-sharing, will be put to the ACTU congress in September and is expected to win approval, with the Labor Party under pressure to support the idea. Page 1.

Senior human rights officials have accused the Australian Government of refusing to allow several senior Cambodian royalist officials, who have been in hiding since last week's coup, to join Friday's RAAF airlift out of the country. The sources also say the Australian embassy in Cambodia has refused to open its doors to any Cambodians but Australian Ambassador to Cambodia Tony Kevin last night refused to comment on the allegations. Page 1.

Former Federal Aviation Support Minister Gary Punch has revealed the details of the Cabinet brawl over the decision to open Sydney's Kingsford Smith airport. Punch has revealed that factional retribution was a factor in the final decision, which subjected hundreds of thousands of Sydney residents to intense aircraft noise and made Sydney Australia's noisiest city. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
